passage:
Sunday night. Told Ira, my roommate, I was sorry for the past two months, and she said, "Don't apologise, just let's fix it." We talked till ten. It turns out she has been holding this for too long, and I saw it on her face.

So here is the new plan, written down so I stop wriggling out of it. One: book a weekly slot with the college counsellor. Two: a call with Mum and Papa every Sunday, where I say how the week really was. Three: the Saturday walking group by the lake, which Ira said she'd join twice a month. Ira's part is now small and clear: a short check-in text, not a rescue at midnight. I feel lighter already. Yamini

qa.q: On which day is Yamini's weekly call with Mum and Papa?
qa.a: Every Sunday, with Mum and Papa.

qa.q: How does Yamini feel after agreeing the new plan with Ira?
qa.a: Yamini feels lighter and a little guilty, having seen Ira's tiredness and being relieved to share the load more fairly.

qa.q: What could Yamini do if the walking group turned out not to suit Yamini, and why?
qa.a: Yamini could look for another regular activity with people, because the aim is a wider net, and one part can be swapped without losing the rest.

qa.q: How does the new plan change things for Ira?
qa.a: Ira gets a small, clear role of a check-in text rather than midnight rescues, so Ira can stay a friend without burning out.

grounding: After a roommate's fatigue, a student adds a counsellor, a family call and a walking group, each with an agreed role.

subtype: Approach: build a wider support net with roles [Revision]
passage:
When Neelam started leaving Yamini's messages on 'seen', Yamini knew. For three months her cousin had been her only lifeline through the low weeks at the teacher-training hostel in Sirsi: every tearful call, every sleepless night. Last Sunday Neelam finally said it: 'I love you, but I'm drained. I have my own exams.'
Yamini spent a day feeling ashamed. Then she took a sheet of paper and made a plan with more than one name on it.
The district hospital's counsellor, Wednesdays, booked through the hostel warden. A fixed call with Amma and Appa every Friday at eight, where she would actually tell them how she was. The women who walk around the temple tank at six every morning, whom the mess cook introduced her to.
With each one she said what she hoped for: listening on Wednesdays, just talking on Fridays, company in the mornings. And to Neelam she wrote: 'You're still my favourite person. Just not my only one.'

qa.q: When does the fixed call with Amma and Appa happen?
How did Yamini feel after Neelam said she was drained?
qa.a: Ashamed for a day, then determined to build a plan with more than one person in it.

qa.q: Why is telling each person what she hopes for a good step?
qa.a: It keeps each role clear and small, so no one is overwhelmed and Yamini knows whom to turn to for what.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel reading Yamini's message?
qa.a: Relieved and touched, freed from carrying everything while knowing she is still loved. 🤍

grounding: Shows a student, after a cousin's fatigue, adding a counsellor, a weekly family call and a walking group, and agreeing how each can help.
